summary: Tzungkuen Wen works in Buddhist studies, completing a PhD at the University of Queensland under Primož Pecenko, Tamara Ditrich, and Chris Kang. He also studied under Yangzhu Xu, Nandasiri Sayadaw, and Sayadaw U Pandita, later holding posts at Fuyan Buddhist Institute and Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.
Ugyen Pelgen is a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He earned a master's degree from Aligarh Muslim University and served as a lecturer of history at Sherubtse College.

Ulrich Pagel specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied under Tadeusz Skorupski, Philip Denwood, and Renate Söhnen-Thieme, and held a post at SOAS University of London attested from 2013 to 2020.

Ulrich Timme Kragh specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, having studied at Karmapa International Buddhist Institute and the University of Copenhagen. His career includes posts at Harvard, Geumgang University, IIAS, the University of Copenhagen, the University of Sydney, and Australian National University.

Ulrich von Wilamowitz-Moellendorff was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. Educated at Bonn and Berlin under Otto Jahn, Moriz Haupt, Johannes Schmidt, and Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker, he held professorial posts at Greifswald (1876-1883), Göttingen (1883-1897), and Berlin (1897-1921).

Ulrike Roesler is a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who earned her PhD from the University of Münster. She taught at the universities of Marburg and Freiburg before becoming Professor of Tibetan and Himalayan Studies at the University of Oxford.

Uma Chakravarti is a historian and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Delhi under D. Devahuti. She served as an educator at Miranda House from 1966 to 1998.

Umakant Premanand Shah was a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. He served at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara, as deputy director and head of the Ramayana Project, and was director at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda from circa 1966 to 1975.

Umesha Mishra was an Indologist and philosopher. He held a post at the University of Allahabad (1923-1955), served as founder secretary of Ganganatha Jha Kendriya Sanskrit Vidyapeetha (1943-1967), and directed the Mithila Institute from circa 1951 to 1956.

Unnikrishnan Payyappallimana specializes in Indology and related studies. After studying at Ayurveda College, Coimbatore, and the University of Amsterdam, he held posts at FRLHT, Amala Institute of Medical Sciences, and the University of Toyama.

Unrai Wogihara was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Taisho University and the University of Strasbourg under Ernst Leumann and Junjirō Takakusu. He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Shukyo University, and Taisho University.
Unsho Shaku was an expert in Buddhist studies who studied at Mount Koya in 1844. He later founded the Juze-kai in 1884, as well as Kairitsu Gakko and Juuzen Hokutsu.

Uranchimeg B. Ujeed works in Buddhist and Iranian/Central Asian studies. She completed her PhD at SOAS University of London and held a post as a Research Associate in the Mongolia and Inner Asia Unit at the University of Cambridge.

Uranchimeg Tsultem specializes in Buddhist studies and art history, earning degrees from Eötvös Loránd University and UC Berkeley. She has held posts at the Mongolian National University of Arts and Culture, National University of Mongolia, and Indiana University Bloomington.

Uranchimeg Tsultemin is a scholar in history/archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. After earning a PhD at the University of California, Berkeley, she served as a lecturer there and as an associate professor at the National University of Mongolia.

Urs App is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology who earned his PhD from Temple University and studied under Yoshitaka Iriya and Seizan Yanagida. He held posts at Hanazono University and several research institutes across Japan and Europe.
Usha Nilsson was an Indologist and linguist who held a faculty position at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where she later became Emeritus Professor of Languages and Cultures of Asia.
Usharbudh Arya was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of London and held a post at the University of Minnesota from circa 1967 to 1973.
Uta Reinöhl is a linguist and Indologist. She held a post at the University of Cologne in 2018 and was appointed Chair of General Linguistics at the University of Freiburg in 2026.

Ute Hüsken is an Indologist and scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. She completed her doctorate under Heinz Bechert at the University of Göttingen and held positions at Göttingen, Heidelberg University, and the University of Oslo.
